code.why: The World's doors are setup, not a vendor API: this life gives them one valid account and asks once for the applications' key. A malformed or duplicate door request is the World's own setup going wrong, answered by this refusal (architecture, Coverage).

This life and the published examples load no scenario. These declarations validate and render a configured World scenario (architecture, Behaviour and Coverage); no unconfigured World reaches them. Conformance separately drives configured scenarios through the official SDK.
Both walks load no scenario; these declarations realize the explicitly configured scenario branch, reached only by a differently configured World (architecture, Behaviour and Coverage).

A client pages a stored completion's messages with the cursor the previous page gave it (its last_id); an after naming no message of the list is a cursor no page gave, a peer's own invention (architecture, Coverage).
The Harness voice session runs in an unconfigured World; only a separately configured scenario fault reaches this error renderer (architecture, Behaviour and Coverage).

An event with no type or a type OpenAI's Realtime client-events reference does not list, and an append whose audio is not base64, are a peer's own malformed frames: every client event the reference lists is served, and a client speaking that vocabulary sends neither (architecture, Coverage).

A file whose metadata a vendor-backed refresh read back from the live account while its bytes stayed at OpenAI: every file a World uploads keeps its bytes in the World's blobs, so only that World holds a file without them (architecture, Coverage).

The coverage walk directly drives the pack fetch in its own fresh Worlds, never the process host. Conformance separately starts this standalone server and verifies HTTP, boot probe and socket upgrade (architecture, Coverage and Conformance).
